generation.instructions: Generate exactly one untouched image-model result for a controlled character-pose experiment. The only references are a standing subject identity and one target skeleton. Preserve the mouse identity, proportions, costume, palette, line quality, viewing direction, and scale from the standing subject. Follow the target skeleton for the pelvis, spine, head, both arms, both legs, and feet. Use the image-generation tool once and return its native pixels without any post-processing.
generation.negative_requirements: Do not generate multiple images. Do not invent a pose from a running reference because no running character image is supplied. Do not omit, merge, or invent limbs. Do not draw skeleton lines, labels, text, a sprite sheet, a turnaround, scenery, shadows, or extra characters. Do not use ImageMagick, sips, Python imaging libraries, resizing, recanvasing, recoloring, quantization, or any other post-processing.
generation.prompt: Draw the same right-facing mouse from the standing subject reference in the target skeleton's running pose. Preserve the green hooded coat, red scarf, brown belt, brown boots, long tail, facial design, and body proportions. Use a plain white background and return one image.

requests.composed_prompt:
Generate exactly one untouched image-model result for a controlled character-pose experiment. The only references are a standing subject identity and one target skeleton. Preserve the mouse identity, proportions, costume, palette, line quality, viewing direction, and scale from the standing subject. Follow the target skeleton for the pelvis, spine, head, both arms, both legs, and feet. Use the image-generation tool once and return its native pixels without any post-processing.

Negative requirements:
Do not generate multiple images. Do not invent a pose from a running reference because no running character image is supplied. Do not omit, merge, or invent limbs. Do not draw skeleton lines, labels, text, a sprite sheet, a turnaround, scenery, shadows, or extra characters. Do not use ImageMagick, sips, Python imaging libraries, resizing, recanvasing, recoloring, quantization, or any other post-processing.

Reference inputs:
Reference 1 (subject-identity): preserve this subject's identity, proportions, design, palette, and identifying landmarks; do not copy the reference layout or pose.
Reference 2 (pose): use only its pose, facing, limb geometry, and ground contact; do not copy its appearance, line style, or background.

Subject request:
Draw the same right-facing mouse from the standing subject reference in the target skeleton's running pose. Preserve the green hooded coat, red scarf, brown belt, brown boots, long tail, facial design, and body proportions. Use a plain white background and return one image.

The two reference images are ordered: (1) the standing character identity and (2) the target skeleton. Preserve the character only from image 1 and use image 2 only for the complete body pose.
Animation frame 4 of 12. Render exactly one fresh right-facing character image. Do not return multiple images, a sheet, turnaround, wireframe, skeleton, or edited reference board.

raw_outputs.revised_prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept
Asset type: single square pixel-art animation frame, frame 4 of 12
Primary request: Generate exactly one fresh image of the same right-facing mouse character from Reference Image 1, performing the exact complete running pose defined by the skeleton in Reference Image 2.
Input images: Reference Image 1 is subject identity only—preserve its mouse identity, facial design, proportions, costume, palette, pixel-art line quality, viewing direction, and character scale; do not copy its standing pose or layout. Reference Image 2 is pose only—follow its pelvis, spine, head, both shoulders/arms/hands, both hips/legs/feet, limb geometry, facing direction, and ground contact; do not copy its colors, skeleton appearance, line style, or background.
Scene/backdrop: plain pure white background only.
Subject: one small anthropomorphic mouse, right-facing, with large pink inner ears, pointed pale muzzle, long thin tail, green hooded coat, red scarf, brown belt, and brown boots. Preserve every identifying landmark and the compact body proportions from Reference Image 1.
Style/medium: crisp low-resolution pixel art matching Reference Image 1 exactly in palette, pixel density, outline treatment, shading, and line quality.
Composition/framing: 1:1 square; one complete full-body character at the same apparent scale as Reference Image 1; place the character so all ears, tail, hands, coat, legs, and boots fit fully inside the canvas. Apply the target skeleton faithfully: torso upright along the red/magenta spine, head at the top looking right; rear/left arm extends horizontally backward to the left; front/right arm bends and reaches down-forward to the right; rear/left leg extends backward-left and bends down at the knee; front/right leg reaches down-forward with the foot contacting the ground in front. Preserve all four distinct limbs and both distinct feet.
Constraints: exactly one character and one animation frame; exact right-facing identity from Image 1; exact whole-body pose and ground contact from Image 2; preserve green hooded coat, red scarf, brown belt, brown boots, long tail, face, proportions, palette, and viewing direction. Native untouched image-model output.
Avoid: multiple images, panels, sprite sheet, turnaround, reference board, skeleton lines, joint markers, labels, text, scenery, shadows, ground line, extra characters, extra limbs, missing limbs, merged limbs, invented limbs, anatomy changes, costume changes, mirrored facing, copied standing pose, or any pose invented from an absent running-character reference.
